userStories.title: Rename the chat finish job to publish with legacy record recovery
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Rename the chat finish job to publish throughout launch, display and storage-facing contracts while keeping old job records readable.

**Motivation** — The name `finish` reads as "take the PR to ready", the job the nax-finish skill does.

**Approach** — **Rename (US-001).** `ChatJobKind` replaces `"finish"` with `"publish"`. Everything keyed by kind follows: the launch schema in `jobs-provider.ts` (tool `nax-jobs__publish`), `LAUNCH_KINDS`, `parseJobInput` and `buildJobArgv` (`job-argv.ts`), `CHAIN_STEP_FIELDS` and `buildChainStepArgv` (`chain-argv.ts`), `stepDefaults` (`workflow-defaults.ts`), `resolveJobOutcome` (`job-outcome.ts`), `prepareFinish` (renamed `preparePublish`) and `approvePrepared` (`jobs-launch.ts`), `stepLabel` (`chain-tools.ts`), `isFeatureJobKind` / `isRunJobKind` (`job-types.ts`), `FooterJob.kind` and `jobPart` (`tui/chat/job-strip.ts`), and `commandOf` (`tui/chat/layout-job.ts`). `commandOf` returns `nax run <target> --publish-only` for a publish job; today it returns `nax finish <target>`, a command that does not exist. The argv is unchanged: `nax run <feature> --publish-only`. `buildJobsInstructions` names `nax-jobs__publish` on its first and eighth lines, and its sixth line's phrase `nax run (including a publish-only finish)` becomes `nax run (including a publish-only run)`; the line count and order stay the same.

Job records written before the rename stay readable. `JOB_KINDS` in `job-store.ts` lists `"publish"` and keeps `"finish"`, the latter only so a legacy record passes `isJobRecord` before it is mapped. `JOB_ID_PATTERN` accepts the prefix `publish` and the legacy prefix `finish`. `readJobRecords` returns a stored record whose `kind` is `"finish"` with `kind: "publish"` and its `id` unchanged. Chain records are audit data and are never read back (`chain-controller.ts`: "disk records are audit data, never activation input"), so they need no compatibility.

**Scope** — In: all named chat-kind discriminants, approval labels, footer/panel strings, instruction-line substitutions and read-time legacy normalization; unchanged real argv includes -f, -d, --headless and profile arguments. Update existing ordered tool-name assertions in chain-tools.test.ts (AC-20), chain-tool-input.test.ts (AC-1/AC-23), test/unit/chat/chat-host-chain.test.ts (both lists), answer-ask-tool.test.ts (AC-3), jobs-provider.test.ts and jobs-launch.test.ts so publish is third and every other entry stays unchanged. Rename the existing #2819 inputs/schema cases in jobs-launch, chain-argv, job-argv, job-outcome and workflow-defaults tests; keep the pending-stories refusal, publish-only card summary, argv, outcome notes, progress and profile-provenance expectations unchanged. Update workflow-builder.test.ts, workflow-builder-chain.test.ts and chat-status.test.ts rename assertions. Add tests only to existing module test files, including job-store, layout-job and chain-tool-card; split by describe block only if a file would pass 650 lines. Out: US-002 no-op refusal and card warnings; US-003 held-draft enrichment/chain stops; US-004 notice guidance; no nax-jobs__finish alias or unrelated finish subsystem rename.

**Interface** — Target ChatJobKind: `"plan" | "run" | "publish" | "bot_review" | "bot_fix"`. Target JOB_ID_PATTERN accepts `plan|run|publish|finish|bot_review|bot_fix` prefixes (`finish` for legacy records only; `newJobId` never produces it). Existing function signatures remain otherwise unchanged.

userStories.title: Guide the chat agent to draft evidence-backed rulings and ask once
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace chain-continuation guidance on held-draft notices with an exact evidence-first, single-approval ruling preparation plan.

**Motivation** — The user's standing requirement is minimal human interaction: finish problems go to an agent, and the user is asked once, only for what the evidence cannot settle.

**Approach** — **Notice guidance (US-004).** `JobNoticeInput` gains `held?: { url?: string; items: readonly { id: string; kind: string }[]; unreadable?: true }`, a structural copy of `HeldDraft` so `prompts` does not import from `chat`. `buildJobNotice` keeps its first two lines. When `held` is present, it adds this line third and leaves out the chain line, because a held draft has stopped the chain:

`The PR is a draft held by <N> open <item|items> (<heldItemList(items, { withKinds: false })>). Do not ask the user to rule on them. Read them with nax workflow status -f <target> --json, then settle each one from evidence as the nax-finish skill's Step 3 does (load it with nax-skills__load when it is listed): verify the item's premise against commits, code and tests, and draft one reply per item whose first line is its ruling keyword (verified:, confirm:, override:, waive: or fixed <sha>) followed by the evidence; findings are left to nax bot fix. Then send the user one message with every drafted reply and the plan (post the replies on their item threads, then nax-jobs__bot_review, then nax-jobs__bot_fix); on their yes, post each reply on its item's thread with gh or glab and propose that chain.`

When `unreadable` is set, the opening reads `The PR is a draft whose open items could not be read.`; when `items` is empty without `unreadable`, it reads `The PR is a draft with no open items listed.`. Both then continue from `Read them with`. `JobRunner` already builds notices from the terminal `ChatJob` record (`buildJobNotice(this.records.get(job.id) ?? terminal)`), so `held` reaches the notice through the record without new wiring.

This line implements the user ruling of 2026-11-17: the agent posts ruling replies on the user's one approval. That replaces slice-2 design §4.7's "agent-only rulings stay with `nax bot fix` and the user". The design document is updated by hand on this branch (see Out of Scope).

**Scope** — In: structural notice input extension, exact third-line wording and three opening variants, singular/plural and the existing US-003 formatter, suppression of chain continuation only when held exists, existing no-held notice preservation, and a runner child-exit integration assertion proving the queued notice receives held from _jobOutcomeDeps. Extend existing prompts/builders/workflow-builder.test.ts and notice-summary.test.ts plus chat/jobs/job-runner.test.ts; restore all outcome-dependency stubs and use existing fake-child/durable-change helpers. No planned new files; split by describe block only if a test would pass 650 lines. Out: US-003 held derivation, formatter creation or chain stopping; US-002 publish refusal/warnings; US-001 rename/instruction-line changes; dedicated reply-posting tools, implementing posting inside JobRunner or posting before the user's yes, koda handoff, permission/session changes and the hand-edited design document. The notice must still instruct the chat agent to post the drafted replies after the user's one approval, as specified above. `buildJobsInstructions` is untouched by this story.

**Interface** — Add to JobNoticeInput the spec's structural field `held?: { url?: string; items: readonly { id: string; kind: string }[]; unreadable?: true }`. Retain buildJobNotice(input: JobNoticeInput): string and reuse heldItemList(items, { withKinds: false }) from US-003; do not introduce a prompts-to-chat dependency. JobRunner's existing terminal-record call is the integration seam, not a new adapter or projection.

analysis:
This is an enhancement of the existing Bun/TypeScript chat-job system in @nathapp/nax, not a greenfield service. All implementation stays in packages/nax; no cross-package dependency or release/version change is needed. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host, so discovery used direct Read, Grep and Glob tools against the supplied execution repository. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:13-35 and :152-172 before implementation: use injectable _deps for external calls, pure prompt builders, explicit constants, Bun APIs, bounded functions and bun:test with restored dependency seams. The binding execution order is US-001 first, US-002 and US-003 each dependent only on US-001, and US-004 dependent only on US-003. Keep exactly these four implementation stories.
